title: Standardising and interpreting a z-score
problem: $X \sim N(60, 25)$, so $\mu = 60$ and $\sigma = 5$. (a) Find the $z$-score for $x = 72.5$. (b) Interpret what this z-score means.

steps.instruction: Part (b): Interpret the z-score, and show how to reverse the process.
steps.working: A z-score of 2.5 means that $x = 72.5$ is 2.5 standard deviations above the mean. You can also reverse the process: if someone tells you $z = -1.4$, the corresponding raw value is: $$x = \mu + z\sigma = 60 + (-1.4)(5) = 60 - 7 = 53$$

answer: $z = 2.5$, meaning $x = 72.5$ is 2.5 standard deviations above the mean.

title: Applying the empirical rule (combining regions)
problem: $X \sim N(100, 64)$, so $\mu = 100$ and $\sigma = 8$. Using the empirical rule, find $P(84 \le X \le 116)$.

steps.instruction: Identify how many standard deviations each endpoint is from the mean.

steps.working: The empirical rule states that in any normal distribution: $$P(\mu - \sigma \le X \le \mu + \sigma) \approx 0.68$$ $$P(\mu - 2\sigma \le X \le \mu + 2\sigma) \approx 0.95$$ $$P(\mu - 3\sigma \le X \le \mu + 3\sigma) \approx 0.997$$ So: $$P(84 \le X \le 116) = P(\mu - 2\sigma \le X \le \mu + 2\sigma) \approx 0.95$$

steps.instruction: Consider the asymmetric case $P(84 \le X \le 108)$, where $108 = \mu + \sigma$, by splitting at the mean.

title: Comparing values across two distributions
problem: Alice sat two exams: English, where her score was 74 against a class mean of 65 and class SD of 12; and History, where her score was 88 against a class mean of 80 and class SD of 6. In which exam did she perform better relative to her class?

steps.instruction: Compare the z-scores to interpret relative performance.
steps.working: Alice's History z-score ($\approx 1.33$) is higher than her English z-score ($0.75$), so she performed better relative to her class in History, even though her raw score in English is closer to the mean in number. The z-score strips away the effect of different means and spreads, making scores from different distributions comparable.

answer: Alice performed better relative to her class in History (z ≈ 1.33) than in English (z = 0.75).
